description:
This benchmark and review of the NVIDIA RTX 2080 Super tests performance vs. the RTX 2080, GTX 1080 Ti, RX 5700 XT, Radeon VII, and more.
Support GN via the store: https://store.gamersnexus.net/

The RTX 2080 Super should be on Amazon here: https://geni.us/O3ga4U4

NVIDIA's RTX 2080 Super places marginally ahead of the RTX 2080, below the 2080 Ti, sort of barely replaces the 1080 Ti, and is utterly boring to review. Enjoy!

Support for RTX tech in 3D modelling and texturing software has rocketed recently. I'm  a hobbyist looking for an RTX card specifically for that reason, and it is likely many architectural firms, freelance, and small studio 3D artists, etc. are looking to upgrade to RTX without going for high priced TI, Titan, or Quadro cards. So while a 1080 may have similar performance for games, it doesn't suit their purposes. But if I got this and choose to game, the 2080 super would  provide a substantial performance boost over my 4 year old RX 480.

comments.text:
Asking AMD to "do something" isn't going to work. It isn't AMD's fault, and technically it isn't NVIDIA's fault either; sure, NVIDIA hiked their prices through the roof, dicked around with product naming, lied about GPU features, etc., but ultimately the people responsible for this mess are the consumers who bought the RTX cards. I talked to one guy who literally said he would pay 100% more for a revised Titan RTX if it was just 5% faster - people like that are killing the GPU market. Having said that, I do wish tech reviewers would stop saying these price point are "ok" because we all know that just isn't true; the prices are far too high, the 60 series now 100% more than it was a few years ago (midrange cards for 400 quid is ridiculous). Also, competition shouldn't be in "price classes", not when people have such distorted perceptions of the products on offer. That's akin to saying consumers should buy an expensive Super card instead of Navi just because the former costs more. :D  The encouraged decision should be about performance and value (cost per frame), with the usual other stuff mixed in like noise, etc. Factor in the used market (Vega56, RX 580, 1080 Ti, etc.) and the entire RTX stack atm is a complete waste of time.


The Super cards are overpriced junk, we all know this is the case, NVIDIA even said in its financial discussions that it had deliberately jacked up the entire stack because they knew ignorant consumers would buy them. Slap an NVIDIA label on it and they will come. AMD is not going to release anything to compete at the high end as long as the mindshare & mindset in the public is so stuck in the mud. No amount of AMD releasing anything is going to help if the consumer perception just isn't there to support it. It's about mindshare and public perception. X-Box Code Scarlett will have 4 times the power of X-Box One X with 120fps 8K released December of 2020 probably at $500. By the end of 2020, sales on gaming PCs will rapidly grow where the market had been stagnant in 2018 from after the huge jump in 2012, with the beginning of major changes in 2019 while the end of 2020 will create much bigger long term financial growth and competition.
